This game is absolutely phenomenal. From the artwork, to the storyline, full voice acting, and the jumpscares. You can tell a lot of love was put into this game and how every choice was planned out to lead the player down certain routes/endings. I really appreciate how each choice has a consequence whether big or small that can influence other characters' routes. It's really interesting to be able to experiment with that and see each of the characters' deaths, good or bad endings and everything between. Even after playing through this game MULTIPLE times there's still lots of content to be had with finding new dialogue and achievements. I HIGHLY recommend this game to anyone interested in a captivating story about a silly, little haunted piece of paper and all of Isabella's friends that get dragged into this.

I hate that I have to give this a thumb down, because some qualities are actually decent. Good art, good animation, full voice acting. But after 3 hours, I just can't stand the dialog anymore. It's not even a slow burn, it's straight up a test of endurance. I bought horror visual novel to learn about a scary mystery, not having to inhale some mundane problems of your boring NPCs. Look at Spirit Hunter series, tight & relevant dialogs, gets you on speed right away while still makes you care about the cast. 

If you are looking for where to start with horror VN, go straight to Sprit Hunter:NG, that's the golden standard.

[h1]Wasted Letters and Potential[/h1]

That's the thought that consistently occurred to me after completing my first playthrough; The Letter is nothing if an utter waste of potential. The entire premise is solid and it starts out strong, hitting you in the face early in with the antagonist; She's not just a myth, she's very real and wasting no time trying to kill the cast. Unfortunately, it simply takes a glorious swan dive off a cliff and unceremoniously splatters itself on the ground. The VN is rife with issues that on their own might be tolerable, but pile up quickly and become quite problematic.


[h2]Illusion of Choice[/h2]
What choice? Your actions don't chantge much, killing characters off changes very little since most branches on the path converge into a single point. Even with 3 of 7 characters dead by Chapter 6, the story simply continues as though they didn't exist, only a sporadic comment about dead characters. For all the choices the game offers you, it all feels remarkably pointless and guided towards the exact same ending every time, even at 57 hours I've only managed to fully complete Chapters 1-5. Chapters 6-7 are unbelievably convoluted with the path branching off at the beginning, then branches forming from the branch, with those branches having branches of their own. All this, with no notation on the already-read nodes to tell you about the route, leaving you to guess or simply utilise a guide to know what arbitrary decision you had to make as far back as Chapter 1. For a novel like this, notation is a requirement to make repeated playthroughs not only enjoyable but actually viable. After reaching 85% completion on Chapter 6, I simply gave up after seeing that the node I was going for was inaccessible because I hadn't made one pointless choice several chapters earlier. I also won't be able to attain the True Ending since it requires you to obtain all Memory Fragments, but I refused to waste several more hours mindlessly skipping text for what will likely amount to the equivalent of being gifted deodorant.

As an extra note: The store page claims it has 700k words, yet there's a branch for each possible character combination during the finale, all of which share the exact same set of base lines and some extra sprinkled in depending on who's present. One can't help but wonder if most are simply duplicates from various branches that get counted as unique text. Food for thought.


[h2]Visuals & Audio[/h2]
For a genre known as "visual novels", you'd think there would've been a little more care put into the art to ensure it's actually consistent. At a first glance, you'll see these well-drawn backgrounds with quite a lot of detail and care put into them. Each area is visually distinct and conveys the atmosphere each should have. The only backgrounds which were a miss were the hideous bloody ones; it's the same background but now it looks like a drunkard chugged red food dye then vomited all over it. The character sprites though?

[b]Like acid to the eyes[/b]

Not only does do the character sprites have a completely different artstyle from both background art [i]and[/i] dialogue sprites, but they're absolutely hideous. It attempts this strange blend of anime/cartoon artstyles and semi-realism, only to completely fail on both fronts and create this lobotomised monstrosity of an artstyle. The only saving grace is that they didn't use this same artstyle throughout, because I genuinely believe most people would rather gouge their eyes out than have to look at that artstyle on a broader scale. It's quite a shame too, as the detailed scenes they have of the characters actually look fantastic (usually) and really give them that pop of personality they're so desperately lacking in their other depictions.

Now, I do understand that to voice an entire visual novel is no small endeavour and is quite a costly one at that, with skilled voice actors requiring a significantly higher budget. However, with how poor the voice work here is? They may as well have not bothered voicing the characters at all, as once again five of seven are just lifeless and lack any personality. The delivery of the lines is, put simply, flat and lifeless. It sounds like the characters are often reading off a script rather than conversation between actual people. Lines feel stiff and forced, inorganic and directed into the microphone rather than the character being spoken to. Tense moments feel overly dramatised due to how characters sounds almost as though they're shouting, when the tone of the conversation is a heated argument at best. Emotional moments feel overly forced and unnatural, as though the characters are simply reacting how they [i]think[/i] they should be reacting to whatever tragic or horrific event has occurred. A character who just saw his childhood best friend reduced to a splattered corpse should should sound devastated, instead he sounds like someone pissed in his cornflakes. Even ignoring the poor delivery of lines, there's a glaring issue with the voices themselves; they simply don't match the characters very well. Why does a Scottish woman sound British 99% of the time, then decide out of nowhere she's going to do a poor imitation of a Scottish accent? Why does a Filipina who's spent five years in Britain sound like she's lived in America most of her life? Minor details, but minor details like this add up and can detract from the readers immersion. All this with some bizarre audio issues to boot: Some lines sound like the VA is too far from the microphone, some lines sound like the VA is too close to the microphone, conversations that are being held over the phone will randomly lose the audio filter, some lines have the incorrect audio file attached.


[h2]Relationships?[/h2]
That's right, there's one last criticism for this novel and it's the atrocious relationship system. Why does a horror novel need a relationship system, you may be asking?

[b]It ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ doesn't.[/b]

The inclusion of this abysmal system is mind boggling and the purpose of it escapes me entirely, yet it's a part of this so I'll give my scathing opinion of it. This is singlehandedly the worst thing in the entirety of the novel, being a complete and utter waste of time designed to do nothing more than pad out your playtime and add to the bragged-about Epilogue count. There's only one character which suffers consequence for getting the relationship status with a specific character to critical levels, but to attain that state requires a specific string of choices you're not likely to achieve on your first playthrough, alongside killing every other character prior to Chapter 7 to attain the associated ending. The rest of the cast suffer no actual consequences if a relationship reaches a negative/critical status beyond "Oh no, friendship fell apart" as an Epilogue scene. Getting relationships to a high enough status between certain pairings can get you a relationship ending, but that's it. Otherwise, the system has no impact at all beyond potentially giving you a few extra lines on some minor branch, but I stopped caring after my fourth playthrough. If only I had the sense to stop caring earlier on.


[h2]The Literary Failure[/h2]
I feel that would be an apt name for this novel, as everything here is a failure and a testament to how difficult it can be to successfully create a good visual novel. Throughout my 57 hours playing this, I couldn't help but find myself thinking I'd rather go read a different visual novel. I can appreciate the attempt here, but ultimately this one fails to be a compelling novel, much less a compelling horror experience. If you want a horror visual novel with branching paths, just go play Raging Loop; it achieves everything The Letter sets out to do, without all the shortcomings.

It took me a LONG time to finally play through this whole game and complete it, but here we are! It's good. Maybe even very good, if you get the True Ending, but I'm not replaying the entire game (even with skips) to experience that. As is, the experience leaves me a little wanting, though from what I've skimmed, there isn't MUCH that I would've gotten from the game that would improve my analysis. 

The game's beautiful. Great voice acting, even if the studio production quality varies. Some good mood music. Animated dolls for the characters AND portraits AND full screen illustrated drawings for dramatic moments. My only complaint is that the character dolls sometimes look TOO MUCH like dolls, their eyes or facial expressions set in a way that seems uncanny.

It's better to live in the moment for the game rather than pondering the mystery, and that's a letdown. There's depth to every one of the seven perspective characters. Characters I love become wretched, characters that disgust me demonstrate a noble nuance, but you can't see every detail of any of it in a single playthrough. To do that, I'd need to restart the game and play through different routes. This is complicated by the fact taht you cannot JUST restart to any of the many, MANY branching path decisions, nor is there a toggle to change the effective decision you made or current relationship level with other characters, going into a scene. I've played at least 15 hours of this game, and I'm not going back any time soon.

The horror pieces were pretty good, with dark and unsettling ambiance, sudden shifts into horror mixed with slow progressions into dread, and some truly unsettling voice work and art for the supernatural. My only complaint are the QTEs that accompany some of these moments. They're frustrating because you're given little time to complete them before your perspective character gets killed off. I'm guessing it's meant to simulate a sense of hurried fear in the player, to replicate how the ghost makes the characters feel, but I found them distracting. Fortunately, you can turn that off.

Overall, I enjoyed my experience with The Letter. Maybe I'll return some day and see all the other paths. But even as-is, I'm happy for the experience.

8/10: I decided to play this game because I loved the other titles from this game studio, including Sait Maker and Love Esquire. I was not disappointed. The story featured in the game is superb. The decisions you make during the game not only have an emmence effect on your current chapter, but also determine how the following chapters play out. This creates a massively branching story tree, with a huge number of possible end-game scenarios.
The game plays in seven chapters, each having a different protagonist. The time lines of the chapters patieally overlap, which sometimes allows vieweign the same events from different perspectives. This also means that high-pace events ending each of the chapters are switched to slow-paced beginning of the next chapter. This might make the game feel slow at times. 
Each chapter has a "good" and a "bad" ending, creating 7! (seven factorial) different end-game combinations. In addition to the "horror" aspect of the game, there is a "romance" aspect. Certain in-game decisions increase/decrease you current character's standing with other characters, which could lead to end-game romance. There are a total of seven different romance options in the game.
Regarding the story itself, given the amount of branching in the game, it is very difficult to get all questions answered in a single play-through. Of all the different end-game combinations, there is only one that is considered "true ending". To achieve it, some of the characters must die in the course of the game. The decisions that lead to each chapter's outcome are not always obvious. THis might make it a surprise how your current character ends up at the end of the chapter.
To summarize, this is another example of a superb game from this studio. The main highligh if of course the story. I am looking forward to playing the next game they release!

Nota: 8,2
- Jogabilidade:
The Letter é uma Visual Novel, e como tal, possui uma jogabilidade voltada para a narrativa, com pequenas ações do jogador para decidir entre uma escolha ou outra, que pode definir o destino dos personagens. Considerando o gênero, a jogabilidade cumpre o seu dever. Ponto extremamente positivo que nem todas as visual novels possuem é a voz dos personagens e a atuação das pessoas talentosas por trás dessas vozes.
- História:
A narrativa é o coração do jogo. É um clássico caso de terror onde os protagonistas precisam entender o motivo por trás de mortes, desaparecimentos e aparições. Um ponto extremamente positivo é a mudança de perspectiva durante o jogo, o que deixa o jogador ansioso para entender o destino do personagem que estava jogando antes da mudança de perspectiva. Os personagens possuem profundidade e são interessantes de se conhecer e entender. 
- Gráficos e Arte:
O estilo artístico complementa o jogo com maestria, sendo brutal e sangrento quando precisa também. O design da aparição é bem grotesca, o que contribui para o sentimento de terror silencioso que o jogador sente cada vez que ela aparece. 
- Som e Trilha Sonora:
Bons atores, que contribuem para a imersão. A trilha sonora, apesar de boa, não é extremamente memorável. 
- Design de Mundo:
Cumpre o seu papel.
- Desempenho Técnico:
Não tive nenhum problema técnico.
- Rejogabilidade:
Moderada. Após uma longa história, o jogador pode se cansar e não ter a vontade de rejogar e verificar como a história seria diferente caso escolhesse uma a opção x em vez da y. Para aqueles dedicados a verificar todos os finais, vale a pena. 
- Imersão:
Com um fone de ouvido de qualidade, você até esquece está jogando. Boa imersão. 
.
- Conclusão:
The Letter não é feita apenas para os fãs de visual novels. Ela é feita para os iniciantes no gênero, com uma história de fácil digestão e relativamente rápida. Para aqueles que estão pensando em iniciar o gênero, é uma ótima pedida. E para aqueles que estão acostumados, esperem uma ótima experiência. Nada como Doki Doki, Raging Loop ou You and Me and Her, mas ainda sim uma ótima experiência para os fãs do gênero e para os amantes de terror. 
A jogabilidade é o que é esperado, o desempenho é ótimo, os personagens são cativantes e as cenas são marcantes. 
Em um churrasco, The Letter seria um contra-filé. Saboroso, mas não é a estrela principal.

Este título destaca por unos valores de producción superiores a la media. La música, las voces, las ilustraciones y los efectos visuales están muy cuidados, lo que contribuye a una experiencia inmersiva y atractiva.

Al estar completamente en inglés, resulta especialmente útil para quienes deseen practicar el idioma, ya que incorpora expresiones de uso común que aparecen de forma natural en los diálogos.

En cuanto a jugabilidad, se reduce a los QTE y a las elecciones que el jugador debe tomar a lo largo de la trama. La obra es extensa y se centra principalmente en las relaciones entre los personajes, aunque esto se hace en detrimento del componente sobrenatural, que termina sin quedar del todo explicado incluso después de completar el juego. Esta amplitud narrativa provoca una pérdida de intensidad y afecta al ritmo general de la historia.

Para facilitar la exploración, se incluye un botón de avance rápido que evita repetir escenas o diálogos ya vistos, así como un árbol de decisiones que permite visualizar las bifurcaciones narrativas y acceder a todo el contenido disponible.

La historia y los personajes recuerdan a producciones de estilo Netflix, con líneas argumentales que, en algunos momentos, parecen responder más a exigencias de financiación o a la intención de desplazar la ventana de Overton en determinados temas que al desarrollo orgánico de la trama. Además, se aprecia una inclusividad forzada que altera el diseño de algunos personajes, a los que se asignan roles preestablecidos que limitan su naturalidad dentro de la narrativa. Aún así, la obra resulta disfrutable y ofrece suficientes alicientes para mantener el interés.

The Letter is a horror visual novel that tells the tale of seven people who fell victim to a malicious curse. Causing them to fall upon a series of hallucinations… or was it real?

[h2] Story [/h2]

The game contains seven extensive chapters, beginning with Isabella’s route as the first chapter. Starting at school, Santos was checking up on her friend, Rebecca Gales just before heading to work as a real estate agent. Her current large sale revolves around the infamous Ermengarde Mansion, located on the outskirts of Luxbourne City. It is rumored to be a haunted ghost paradise lurking about. Even various disappearances had been linked to the mansion. The usual cliche ghost stories, nothing special. However, Isabella’s unfortunate fate leaves her noticing a bloodied-up letter filled with two words; “Help me” which fills half the paper, and ending with the sentence “Send this to 5 people or else…” It is after this letter that the other six characters unexpectedly become cursed too. The plot even brings up their past traumas, troubled situations, their relationship, and how each character gets to meet the other even if they don’t relate entirely. Additionally, there’s a whole story behind the mansion and its original owners, though I didn’t get to know the whole details [spoiler] due to causing characters to die in certain branches. [/spoiler]

[h2] Atmosphere [/h2]

The vibrant CGs show a sense of life and sometimes coziness, yet they deliver horror and gore. The art for both backgrounds and characters is nothing short of astounding. I also noticed such beautiful details for various items such as foods! 

[h2] Characters & Voice Acting [/h2]

The starting route order will be as follows: Isabella Santos, Hannah Wright, Zachary Steele, Marianne McCollough, Rebecca Gales, Ashton Frey, and Luke Wright. These are the main characters, along with a few minor ones. In each character's route, we will have access to their stream of consciousness in every event they experience with the others. In simpler terms, we get to see their perspective. There are clear options for both friendship and romance among the various characters.

I usually don't focus much on voice acting in my reviews, but in this case, it stands out fantastically. The voice acting is truly exceptional and is one of the reasons I kept playing. I especially loved the voice of Hannah Wright, portrayed by Amber Lee Connors. Her voice is soft, soothing, and elegant. It’s similar to my favorite British actress Billie Piper (fan since Doctor Who days). I'm not belittling other voice actors; they all delivered high-quality performances equally, and I particularly enjoyed Hannah's and Ashton's routes.

[h2] Gameplay [/h2]

[i] Tap… tap… ttaapp [/i]

It’s a visual novel there’s nothing to do. It’s effortless, but there are QTEs, and it differentiates each time one occurs. You can choose to skip it though. Moreover, there is an extensive range of outcomes depending on the choices made in response to various situations. Each response can lead to multiple endings and affect relationships. A single choice may result in a positive or negative outcome for each character, or it could have a positive impact on one character while negatively impacting another.

[h2] Conclusion and Final Thoughts [/h2]

I really enjoyed it. Nevertheless, it didn’t hook me. The horror part in particular, it’s cheesy. It’s rather an otome for me. I liked the characters and their backgrounds. The writers did absolutely great with each one, which is why I continued to play because I got a huge crush on Ashton Frey, and partly because I wanted to see where my choices would lead, which happened to be a good ending in my opinion. The most boring routes for me were Marianne’s and Rebecca’s. I struggled to finish them the most. I had an expectation however before purchasing it that they’ll be trapped together in the mansion or something; sort of like Corpse Party in that regard. It did but only briefly in the final chapter. Yet the outcome did impress me too nonetheless. 

As I’ve mentioned before, the voice acting influenced me too. It is marvelous! There were quite a bit details that annoyed me, but at the end of the day, I chose not to recommend it not because it is unworthy, oh believe me it certainly is if you want to consider it as an otome. Besides, I wouldn’t have spent 43 hours over it as a VN enjoyer. Anyway, the reason is that it didn’t deliver the horror part right. At least that’s what I think. It’s not scary at all and through my playthough I never once said (that’s fu*cked up) to myself which is something I always like to say when I see or read crazy sh*it (excuse my language I’m excited writing this lol). Back to the point, the amount of horror was less than the average and more like slice of life yaddi yadda.

All in all, it’s decent. Great characters, writing, voice acting, illustrations, and nice soundtracks. However, it’s weak in terms of horror. It has the elements set correctly but not the action for me. I would recommend it if anyone would prefer “romance horror VN” otherwise, I wouldn’t. There are better ones such as Death Mark.

给太长不看的人：这个游戏是个优秀的GAL，同时是一个糟糕的恐怖游戏：日常和恋爱的情节写的很出色，人物塑造立体，好感度分支系统很有意思，画面优秀，音乐优秀，配音优秀；但是恐怖氛围为零，主线烂俗且冗长，叙事方式极其糟糕，jumpscare不存在的，吓人的水平仅次于俄罗斯方块。

下面是正文：

首先首先首先，这游戏最令我不满的地方就是true end的设定，要达成真结局，必须要死三个人，而且每死一个人就会解锁一个记忆碎片，告诉你一段真相。而你要是全员存活通关了，反而到头来啥都不知道。这应该是我玩过的第一个鼓励死主角的游戏，制作组的想法真的太迷了。当然我知道恐怖游戏不死人不可能的，如果是剧情杀的话我完全可以接受，但是让玩家控制主角去送死？（何况那几个主角根本没有该死的地方）我反正做不到。

抱着这种想法，我最后去看了真结局的剧透，然后发现——这剧情TM和我猜的一毛一样啊，就是一个人杀了ta全家，然后死人的怨气盘踞在死的地方，无差别的把所有踏进那凶宅的人给杀了。不要觉得我在剧透，因为我只是在复述十几年前一个叫《咒怨》的鬼片的剧情罢了。说到这里，我觉得制作组里肯定有咒怨的大粉丝，具体的原因我放到后面说吧。话说回来，你要借鉴某个老掉牙的日本鬼片的剧情倒不是不行，但是强行加上一个美式主旋律鬼片的结局就很扯淡了。 这帮菲律宾人根本不懂亚洲鬼片的精髓啊。

然后，这游戏的恐怖场景少得可怜，制作组不但不擅长描写恐怖场景（词汇量匮乏，铺垫太过明显缺少突然感，CG画的不错可惜游戏内的演出效果一塌糊涂，QTE？不存在的，整个游戏只有七章，QTE加起来大概也只有七个），绝大多数剧情都是日常——导致的结果就是，这游戏不但根本吓不到人，反而一度让我产生在推GAL的错觉（狗粮真好吃）。听说制作组的下一个游戏是带恋爱元素的RPG？幸好他们及时发现了自己对恋爱模拟游戏是多么擅长，让他们做恐怖游戏真是屈才了（误）。不过我这句话并非完全开玩笑，尽管游戏的主线剧情非常糟糕，但是游戏在塑造人物和情感描写方面不可否认非常出色，好感度分支方面也做的非常好，要是制作组去做一款正常向的GAL肯定比现在这个“恐怖游戏”要好多了。

最后一点，和上面那点讲的其实是同一回事，这游戏的叙事节奏不行，给人一种冗余感——无聊的铺垫太多，高潮又结束的太快。
而剧情本身的结构也很有问题，比如第三章结尾的时候游戏主线实际上已经小高潮了，但是突然插进来一个突兀的第四章，和主线一点关系都没有，第二章也给人一样的感觉，再比如第三章和第五章非常相似，完全可以删掉其中一章。要我说这游戏七章的剧情其实四章就可以讲完，一三（五）六七。至于为什么要把剧情拖这么长，大概因为作者有强迫症，每个主角一定要有一章，所以就变成七章了。（说到底，主角为什么一定要是七个人啊，要我说玛丽安这个角色完全是冗余的）

基于以上四点，我认为此游戏作为Horror Visual Novel是不合格的。

此外，这点八成是我自己的好恶问题，因为这游戏的文风真的很难受，总是喜欢在对话中间插大段心理描写，很容易让人跟不上原本的对话，再加上游戏本身的词汇还是偏难的， 也就是GRE的词汇水平吧，顺带中间插几句法语，读着是真的累，而很不巧的是，这个游戏文本量奇大。

好了批评完了，下面说优点：
这游戏的美术、音乐、配音，还有上面说过的，GAL元素和人物的塑造，每一点都非常精良。
特别要提一下游戏的配音，而且是全对话配音，真的非常棒，我特别喜欢伊莎贝拉的哭腔，还有卢克在挑衅的时候和发毛的时候的声音，可以听出CV是非常代入角色的；此外玛丽安的爱尔兰口音，瑞贝卡的苏格兰口音，还有管家的德国口音都非常还原，再次强调一遍，配音非常棒。
至于游戏的画风，有个很迷的地方，PV和笔记本里都是日式画风，但是立绘和CG都是美式画风，当然这不是什么问题就是了，要是一群日式画风的人一开口就是流利的英语那才是大大的违和感。此外，这游戏的立绘和CG会动啊，虽然不是live2D，不过制作之精良也很让人感动了。

最后最后最后，我一开始说到了制作组里肯定有咒怨的大粉，因为这游戏的咒怨梗真的太多了，虽然也有其他鬼片的梗（比如贞子钻电视的梗），但是咒怨梗绝对是最多最明显的。除了剧情完全照抄咒怨之外，还有几个地方：每一章开头会显示主角的姓名、女鬼的外表和爬的移动方式（这两点不一定，因为这种设定挺常见的）、女鬼登场时发出的“啊……啊啊”的声音（给不知道的人科普一下，这种声音是被割喉的人发出的）、女鬼钻被窝（可惜没见到下楼梯）。

叙事很枯燥，大量无人在意的日常和感情戏和几近于无的推理，靠着对真相的好奇坚持到最后也很失望……好浅薄无趣的故事

Just finished playing this and got like 2/3 of the total achievements, I've seen multiple good and one true ending and maybe I'll come back to collect the rest of the achievements in the future... or maybe not. Anyway, I think this VN had a lot of heart put into it, from the gorgeous art to the branching choices to the music (although less memorable than other VNs I've read). Here's a few things I liked and disliked about the Letter.

The Letter managed to write natural and convincing characters. Each character have their own unique take on the situation and their thought process rarely feel similar to one another. And don't forget about the art. The art is gorgeous and special. I'm glad the studio didn't go for the standard VN art and stick to something more westernized. The animated backgrounds/characters shows how much effort was put in and I applaud them for that. 

Voice acting is a hit and miss. The over reacting and the higher pitched voices can be a bit of a displeasure to listen to at times. And almost everybody is overacting which is okay if it feels "right" but the characters aren't written that way. And the horror is kinda bad too, after ten times of seeing the ghost's face, most of us probably just didn't care anymore and find her more of an annoyance than a surprise. The QTEs didn't help either. I'm sure the studios put it in for the game to be more marketable but it became the downside after a while. A good horror is mostly about the atmosphere after all, and the Letter failed to deliver one.

Well to cut it short, honestly, I don't hate the Letter. In fact, I really liked it. I admired the effort put into it and love parts of it. [i]The Letter[/i] is an incredibly large visual novel—my first playthrough alone took around 19 hours to complete. While there certainly is a lot of reading, the whole thing is fully voice-acted (with great actors), which helps a lot. It wasn't until my second playthrough, however, that I truly realized just how much this story could drastically change. A character I assumed to be essential to the plot the first time around was written out in my second playthrough with just a couple of bad choices, and the game didn't abruptly end with a non-standard game over (or gloss over their ensuing absence). Instead, it continued, with their loss factoring into the continuing story in a way that almost felt as if it was meant to happen. I was also convinced at the time that characters I lost the first time around were meant to go with how naturally the story played out without them—only to find out in subsequent playthroughs that their loss was not necessary at all.

Achievement hunters will love finding all the ways they can shape the story, with dozens of achievements to earn for doing so. Completionists, however, will likely find exploring every possible path in the final two chapters to be quite difficult. Fortunately, the developers have included plenty of quality-of-life features to help with doing all of this. An option to [i]instantly[/i] skip all previously-seen text up until the next choice (allowing playthroughs to potentially be completed in mere minutes!), a branching tree to track what choices have been made while showing what choices remain to be made, and a gallery of all that you've seen thus far are all very helpful.

Okay, first of all, yes, this game is long, but it took me 300 hours because I mostly played it in Chinese, and I'm not very good at Chinese. Well, I'm a lot better now thanks to this game, but anyway, your playtime should be much lower.

Anyway... is it a well-written, well-developed story with halfway relatable characters? Not really. Is it a fun, campy horror visual novel with good production value and A TON of choice? Yes. It's a (mostly) well-designed game with high production value, good art, and a sufficiently interesting plot with more branches than you can imagine brought down by unlikeable characters, poor writing, bad grammar, and the worst voice acting direction I've ever seen. If you're looking for a campy horror story with tons of choice and don't mind unreasonably long monologues, this is your game.

GOOD:

・The art. There are different art styles for the characters in different contexts (e.g., other characters you're talking to, your character's icon when they're talking, epilogue art), but they're all good. It's a very polished, nice-looking game overall. Luke has an annoying little line on his face when you're talking to him, but otherwise, the art is great.

・The choice. There are TONS of branches. Pretty much every choice matters, either giving you a different ending or changing the characters' relationships. Sometimes the relationship questions are ridiculously obvious and sometimes it seems completely arbitrary which option is the "good" one, but choices certainly matter.

・The branch tree. You get a nice visual for each chapter of all the choices and branches, which is such a great idea. It was quite poorly implemented, but I love the idea.

・The story. Well, there are a lot of problems with the story, and the writing is quite bad, but it's fun as a game. It would not be a good book, but it's good as a game. The characters (might?) grow on you. 

・The soul. It's a labor of love, and you can tell. I have a lot of qualms with the game, but I can appreciate that the devs poured their hearts into it, and I did have a great time with it.


BAD:

・The repetition. Chapters 1, 2, and 4 are basically fine. Chapters 3 and 5 have some annoying repetition. Chapter 6 has a ton of repetition, and Chapter 7 is MOSTLY repetition. My guess is the visual branch tree design caused this because there's limited space to visually represent all the possible nodes, but the game won't recognize identical text on a different node as read, so you'll find yourself having to manually skip text ALL THE TIME once you're far enough in. 

・The grammar. Forget a professional proofreader, this game didn't even get checked by a halfway competent native English speaker. You'll hardly go two lines without encountering some sort of mistake. I played most of the game in Chinese, but I did switch to English at the end, so I could still get a good picture of the English quality.

・The voice acting direction. Johannes and Ashton are the only characters with consistently good voice acting. Rebecca, Marianne, and Zach are consistently awful. Other than Kylie, who sounds like an adult exaggerating the squeakiest, most annoying kid voice in the world, I don't think the voice actors themselves are necessarily bad. I think it's just godawful direction, because the tone always seems at least 10 times more intense than the context. Rebecca and Marianne sound like they overreact with blind fury to literally everything and Zach sounds so annoyingly dense most of the time.

・The characters. I'm not sure what the devs were going for, but I don't think the characters are that likable. Ashton was the only one I consistently liked, but it seems like a lot of people don't like him, and the writers certainly villianize him every chance they get. The game gaslit me for 300 hours about Rebecca being "patient," even though she routinely starts yelling at her friends for no reason at all. Zach is really annoying because the writers won't stop doting on him. Even a character who hates him still says about him, in his first-person narration, "What little anger he is capable of feeling is clear on his face, lining his soft and kind features." Come oooon, is that how you would think about someone you hate? Really?

・The writing. It has all the typical trappings of amateurish writing, including unnecessarily pretentious vocabulary, semicolon misuse, overuse of italics, and inappropriate use of epithets (i.e., random descriptors for familiar people -- e.g., a guy in a first-person narration randomly referring to his wife as "the woman" instead of "she" or her name. Excuse me, do you have amnesia...?). Also, even though the characters have distinct voices in their dialogue, their first-person narration all sounds exactly the same. And the pacing, good god. I'm absolutely here for a slow psychological horror, but the monologues ramble on and on and oooon, bludgeoning you with boring and unnecessary details as you patiently or impatiently wait for something to finally happen. The dialogue is often similarly clunky, especially from Zach and somewhat Luke. 


But for all my grievances in 300 hours of this game, I really enjoyed it. It was a good experience and a very promising start for this studio. So, yes, I can recommend it. Thank you, devs, for all the hard work and love you poured into this game and for the grade-A Chinese lesson.
